relatedScope: Owner-approved distinct federal/state/county/municipal laws; policy-level routing follow-through

phlTax.locator: Who pays the tax; tax-rate table; Did you know

findings.finding: Ohio municipal corporations may levy income/withholding taxes subject to chapter limits. The enactment specifies income base, rate, credit, purpose and administration. Resident credits for tax paid elsewhere can be partial.
findings.limit: Not a complete tax profile; additional restrictions, exemptions and current local ordinance must be applied. Does not establish county authority.

findings.finding: Philadelphia describes its Earnings Tax and employer-withheld Wage Tax as the same tax with different collection treatment. Resident/nonresident applicability and dated rate changes are separately stated.
findings.limit: These are rate-table entries, not universal effective law elsewhere or every exception; January 2026 must not consume the July 2026 rate without a fictional-law record.

receiving: Permit municipal income-tax subject discovery where an actual authority profile supports it. Preserve existing namespace/issue and authored-position references. Do not globally mark every local government competent.
Bind the particular government, taxpayer, income-source/residence nexus, period, taxable base, rate/exemptions/credits, collector and receiving treasury.
Withholding and direct remittance settle the same liability; a wage label plus an earnings label must not collect twice.
An intergovernmental remittance is not another receipt from the household, and one jurisdiction changing its levy cannot overwrite federal/state/other-local instruments.
Topic grouping is not power, passage is not collection, liability is not payment, and observed publication date is not operative date.
